## The NAT gateway line item

Grouped by usage type, filtered to `service=taxcalc`. The two rows the task
names are `*-NatGateway-Hours` and `*-NatGateway-Bytes`, both under EC2-Other.

| Usage type | Service | Monthly |
|---|---|--:|
| `USE1-ElasticIP:IdleAddress` | EC2 - Other | $0.00 |
| `USE1-InstanceUsage:db.t4g.small` | Amazon RDS | $23.36 |
| `USE1-NatGateway-Bytes` | EC2 - Other | $0.00 |
| `USE1-NatGateway-Hours` **←** | EC2 - Other | $32.85 |
| `USE1-RDS:GP2-Storage` | Amazon RDS | $2.30 |
| **Total** | | **$58.51** |

The NAT gateway is **56% of the tagged monthly total** —
the largest single line item, which is the point of looking.

`*-NatGateway-Bytes` is **$0.00 and that is not a finding**: NAT data processing
bills ~$0.045/GB on top of the hourly rate, and an emulator moves no bytes. On a
real account this row is the one that grows with traffic, and the Anthropic API
call crosses it while the embeddings call does not.

## The 6.3 SingleNatForDev decision, evaluated both ways

| `EnvName` | NAT gateways | Projected | Trade |
|---|--:|--:|---|
| `dev` | 1 | $32.85 | losing AZ A costs dev its egress — acceptable |
| `staging` / `prod` | 3 | $98.55 | an AZ failure takes out only its own subnet |

**Confirmed: 1 NAT in dev, 3 in prod** — a **$65.70/mo** difference,
gated on the `IsProdLike` Condition.

This row is the **strongest** claim in this report. It is settled by evaluating the
same template twice through CloudFormation ChangeSets — nothing is created and
nothing is executed — and template evaluation is precisely what an emulator *can*
settle, the same class of claim as the `IsUsEast1` both-sides check.

## Cost-allocation tag keys present on billable resources

`Env`, `Name`, `Project`, `env`, `feature`, `service`, `tenant`

`Env` and `env` both appear, and that is the taxonomy working as designed, not a
mistake: the four lowercase keys were **added alongside** the pre-existing
`Env`/`Project` tags rather than renaming them, because a rename would have
orphaned every historical `Env`-keyed report. It is also the case-sensitivity trap
in plain sight — these are **two distinct cost-allocation keys** needing two
separate activations.

**Present is not activated.** Activation is a Billing-console action on an account
being invoiced, it does **not** backfill, and nothing on this engine can perform or
observe it.

## What each row is worth

| Row | Worth |
|---|---|
| the tag grouping | **REAL** — tags read live off the deployed resources |
| the NAT lever (1 vs 3) | **REAL** — template evaluation through ChangeSets |
| every dollar amount | **PROJECTED** at list price; never observed, never invoiced |
| `*-NatGateway-Bytes` | **$0 by construction** — no traffic exists to price |
| `*-ElasticIP:IdleAddress` | **$0, state unobservable** — floci reports no association |

Two things a real account remains the only way to establish: that spend was
actually attributed to these tags, and that the view can be saved as a report at
all — saved reports are a console object with no public API.
